jp: 友達[ともだち]「この三[みっ]つのプランの中[なか]で、{どれ|ko-dore}がいいと思[おも]う？」。
en: Friend: "Which of these three plans do you think is best?"
why: Choosing one out of a group of things already in view, with no noun following, is どれ.

jp: 友達[ともだち]「来週[らいしゅう]の{どの|ko-dore}日[ひ]が空[あ]いてる？一緒[いっしょ]に映画[えいが]を見[み]に行[い]こうよ。」。
en: Friend: "Which day next week are you free? Let's go see a movie together."
why: A question word placed directly before a noun to pick one out of known options is どの.

jp: 土曜日[どようび]と日曜日[にちようび]、{どちら|ko-dore}のほうが都合[つごう]がいいですか。
en: Saturday or Sunday: which one suits you better?
why: Choosing between exactly two things named in the sentence takes どちら.

jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]の旅行[りょこう]は、{どんな|ko-dore}ところに行[い]きたい？海[うみ]とか山[やま]とか。
en: For the weekend trip, what kind of place do you want to go to? The sea, the mountains, or something else?
why: The question asks about the kind or type of place, not a pick from a known set, so it is どんな.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]に同[おな]じような傘[かさ]が三本[さんぼん]あります。友達[ともだち]「僕[ぼく]の傘[かさ]は{どれ|ko-dore}だと思[おも]う？」。
en: There are three similar umbrellas by the front door. Friend: "Which one do you think is mine?"
why: A pronoun asking which one of several things in view, ending the clause with だ, is どれ.

jp: メニューに料理[りょうり]が十種類[じゅっしゅるい]もあって、{どの|ko-dore}料理[りょうり]にするか迷[まよ]っています。
en: There are ten dishes on the menu, and I can't decide which one to have.
why: The noun 料理 follows directly and the pick is from the dishes on the menu, so it is どの.
